_purpose: THE GROUNDING LAW's escape hatch, and the only one. A proper noun in game text must resolve to something the player can walk up to - a world grid location, a quest title, a spawned NPC, an item, a faction, a god - or it must appear here with the bible line that sanctions it. tools/validate_content.gd::_check_grounded_references() reads this file and nothing else.
_law: Nothing goes on this list to make a number move. An entry is a promise that the reference is DELIBERATELY unresolvable - lore the world talks about but does not contain - and it carries the bible section that says so. A phantom place somebody invented is not lore-only; it is a bug, and the fix is to delete it or replace it with a real place.
_shape: entries[] = {token, reason, bible}. token is matched case-insensitively against a single capitalised word. Multi-word names are listed word by word, because the lint works on tokens.

_offscreen_purpose: The second and last excuse. These are things the world SPEAKS of but does not contain, found by THE GROUNDING LAW's first run on 8/2 in prose that predates it: a battle fought before the game starts, a boat already on the bottom, a book stolen off a shelf. They are not places the player can be sent to and not people the player is told to find - a quest that DIRECTS you at a name gets the name fixed, not excused.
_offscreen_law: Every row names the file that says it and what would make it real. Anything here that later gets a cell on the map, an item, or an NPC comes OFF this list in the same commit. Rows are recorded in docs/audits/wave_b_dispositions.md; this is not a place to park work.

offscreen.reason: The Siege of Blackmont - where Katrina Steelwind's predecessor took an arrow to the throat. A battle fought before the game begins, spoken of once, as a soldier's history. No cell, and it should not have one.

The Ironpeak foothills, north of the mining camps - where a wyvern nest is said to be. This one is a direction, not a memory, and is the weakest row here: if the nest ever becomes a place the player travels to, this reference must be re-pointed at the real cell.

The Ashgrave Cantos, the tome stolen off the Athenaeum's restricted shelf. Already logged as an invention in docs/audits/invention_manifest.md - the quest's own note says so. It is a book in someone else's hands, never an item the player holds.
The Merrow's Kiss, the last boat out of Larton harbour before the mist ship started showing at dawn. A wreck, not a vessel; the quest is about the two brothers who did not come back.
